claims.claim: **Strongyloides is tiny (up to 2 mm) but can keep reproducing inside the body for years unless it is treated.** It is often silent; when it does cause symptoms these include foul-smelling diarrhoea, abdominal pain, poor appetite and constipation.
claims.locator: Central Australian Aboriginal Congress, CARPA, CRANAplus and Flinders University (Remote Primary Health Care Manuals), 'CARPA Standard Treatment Manual, 8th edition (e-version V1.03): Worms, Strongyloides testing, treatment and follow-up (pp 494-498), with the HTLV-1 and COPD cross-references', 8th edition 2022, V1.03 reprinted with corrections May 2026 (Table 7.39 updated June 2024), https://remotephcmanuals.com.au/document/35499.html, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Other signs are a rash that visibly moves from hour to hour, itchy hives over the lower back or buttocks, cough, wheeze or coughing up blood, and low potassium (particularly in young children).**
claims.locator: Central Australian Aboriginal Congress, CARPA, CRANAplus and Flinders University (Remote Primary Health Care Manuals), 'CARPA Standard Treatment Manual, 8th edition (e-version V1.03): Worms, Strongyloides testing, treatment and follow-up (pp 494-498), with the HTLV-1 and COPD cross-references', 8th edition 2022, V1.03 reprinted with corrections May 2026 (Table 7.39 updated June 2024), https://remotephcmanuals.com.au/document/35499.html, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Death is rare but happens two ways:** severe secondary infection (bloodstream, pneumonia, meningitis) or disseminated hyperinfection, where a massive worm load spreads through the body in someone whose immunity is weakened: HTLV1 infection, corticosteroids for over 2 weeks, chemotherapy or transplant drugs.
claims.locator: Central Australian Aboriginal Congress, CARPA, CRANAplus and Flinders University (Remote Primary Health Care Manuals), 'CARPA Standard Treatment Manual, 8th edition (e-version V1.03): Worms, Strongyloides testing, treatment and follow-up (pp 494-498), with the HTLV-1 and COPD cross-references', 8th edition 2022, V1.03 reprinted with corrections May 2026 (Table 7.39 updated June 2024), https://remotephcmanuals.com.au/document/35499.html, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **HTLV-1 is associated with severe strongyloides and scabies infections,** as well as with bronchiectasis, uveitis and infective dermatitis.
claims.locator: Central Australian Aboriginal Congress, CARPA, CRANAplus and Flinders University (Remote Primary Health Care Manuals), 'CARPA Standard Treatment Manual, 8th edition (e-version V1.03): Worms, Strongyloides testing, treatment and follow-up (pp 494-498), with the HTLV-1 and COPD cross-references', 8th edition 2022, V1.03 reprinted with corrections May 2026 (Table 7.39 updated June 2024), https://remotephcmanuals.com.au/document/35499.html, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Test for strongyloides only when:** symptoms suggest it; before starting any treatment that may weaken immunity (including corticosteroids planned for at least 2 weeks); or when there is a systemic infection with a gut organism and no other cause has been found.
claims.locator: Central Australian Aboriginal Congress, CARPA, CRANAplus and Flinders University (Remote Primary Health Care Manuals), 'CARPA Standard Treatment Manual, 8th edition (e-version V1.03): Worms, Strongyloides testing, treatment and follow-up (pp 494-498), with the HTLV-1 and COPD cross-references', 8th edition 2022, V1.03 reprinted with corrections May 2026 (Table 7.39 updated June 2024), https://remotephcmanuals.com.au/document/35499.html, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Serology is the simplest test in adults with symptoms that could be chronic strongyloidiasis,** but immunosuppressed people with disseminated infection can test serology-negative.
claims.locator: Central Australian Aboriginal Congress, CARPA, CRANAplus and Flinders University (Remote Primary Health Care Manuals), 'CARPA Standard Treatment Manual, 8th edition (e-version V1.03): Worms, Strongyloides testing, treatment and follow-up (pp 494-498), with the HTLV-1 and COPD cross-references', 8th edition 2022, V1.03 reprinted with corrections May 2026 (Table 7.39 updated June 2024), https://remotephcmanuals.com.au/document/35499.html, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **In children a faeces test usually works better:** a child with bowel symptoms probably has a recent infection and may not yet be seropositive.
claims.locator: Central Australian Aboriginal Congress, CARPA, CRANAplus and Flinders University (Remote Primary Health Care Manuals), 'CARPA Standard Treatment Manual, 8th edition (e-version V1.03): Worms, Strongyloides testing, treatment and follow-up (pp 494-498), with the HTLV-1 and COPD cross-references', 8th edition 2022, V1.03 reprinted with corrections May 2026 (Table 7.39 updated June 2024), https://remotephcmanuals.com.au/document/35499.html, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Send faeces as fresh as possible and keep it cool, not refrigerated** (heat and cold kill the worms), requesting OCP, MC&S and a strongyloides culture, which not every laboratory offers.
claims.locator: Central Australian Aboriginal Congress, CARPA, CRANAplus and Flinders University (Remote Primary Health Care Manuals), 'CARPA Standard Treatment Manual, 8th edition (e-version V1.03): Worms, Strongyloides testing, treatment and follow-up (pp 494-498), with the HTLV-1 and COPD cross-references', 8th edition 2022, V1.03 reprinted with corrections May 2026 (Table 7.39 updated June 2024), https://remotephcmanuals.com.au/document/35499.html, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Positive faeces test: treat, with ivermectin as the drug of choice. Positive serology: get a medical consult before treating,** because the result can be hard to interpret and underlying or complicating factors need to be looked for.
claims.locator: Central Australian Aboriginal Congress, CARPA, CRANAplus and Flinders University (Remote Primary Health Care Manuals), 'CARPA Standard Treatment Manual, 8th edition (e-version V1.03): Worms, Strongyloides testing, treatment and follow-up (pp 494-498), with the HTLV-1 and COPD cross-references', 8th edition 2022, V1.03 reprinted with corrections May 2026 (Table 7.39 updated June 2024), https://remotephcmanuals.com.au/document/35499.html, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Ivermectin, for adults and children aged 5 years or more who weigh at least 15 kg: 200 microgram/kg by mouth as a single dose, repeated in 1–2 weeks.** Give it with full-cream milk or fatty food.
claims.locator: Central Australian Aboriginal Congress, CARPA, CRANAplus and Flinders University (Remote Primary Health Care Manuals), 'CARPA Standard Treatment Manual, 8th edition (e-version V1.03): Worms, Strongyloides testing, treatment and follow-up (pp 494-498), with the HTLV-1 and COPD cross-references', 8th edition 2022, V1.03 reprinted with corrections May 2026 (Table 7.39 updated June 2024), https://remotephcmanuals.com.au/document/35499.html, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Albendazole, for children aged 6 months to 4 years: by mouth once a day for 3 days, then the 3-day course repeated in 1–2 weeks.** 200 mg if 6–11 months and under 10 kg; 400 mg if 6–11 months and 10 kg or over, or 1–4 years and under 15 kg, or pregnant after the 1st trimester. Give with breastmilk (under 1 year), full-cream milk or fatty food.
claims.locator: Central Australian Aboriginal Congress, CARPA, CRANAplus and Flinders University (Remote Primary Health Care Manuals), 'CARPA Standard Treatment Manual, 8th edition (e-version V1.03): Worms, Strongyloides testing, treatment and follow-up (pp 494-498), with the HTLV-1 and COPD cross-references', 8th edition 2022, V1.03 reprinted with corrections May 2026 (Table 7.39 updated June 2024), https://remotephcmanuals.com.au/document/35499.html, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Get a medical consult before giving albendazole to a child under 6 months or in the first trimester, or ivermectin to a child under 5 years or under 15 kg or in pregnancy;** use a urine pregnancy test if pregnancy is uncertain.
claims.locator: Central Australian Aboriginal Congress, CARPA, CRANAplus and Flinders University (Remote Primary Health Care Manuals), 'CARPA Standard Treatment Manual, 8th edition (e-version V1.03): Worms, Strongyloides testing, treatment and follow-up (pp 494-498), with the HTLV-1 and COPD cross-references', 8th edition 2022, V1.03 reprinted with corrections May 2026 (Table 7.39 updated June 2024), https://remotephcmanuals.com.au/document/35499.html, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **For people from a high-prevalence area (remote communities, some town camps) who are on, or about to start, immune-weakening treatment: treat for strongyloides even when blood and faeces tests are negative.** Treat before the treatment starts and then every 3 months for as long as it continues.
claims.locator: Central Australian Aboriginal Congress, CARPA, CRANAplus and Flinders University (Remote Primary Health Care Manuals), 'CARPA Standard Treatment Manual, 8th edition (e-version V1.03): Worms, Strongyloides testing, treatment and follow-up (pp 494-498), with the HTLV-1 and COPD cross-references', 8th edition 2022, V1.03 reprinted with corrections May 2026 (Table 7.39 updated June 2024), https://remotephcmanuals.com.au/document/35499.html, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Someone whose immunity is already weakened may need 4 or more ivermectin doses;** that is a medical-consult decision.
claims.locator: Central Australian Aboriginal Congress, CARPA, CRANAplus and Flinders University (Remote Primary Health Care Manuals), 'CARPA Standard Treatment Manual, 8th edition (e-version V1.03): Worms, Strongyloides testing, treatment and follow-up (pp 494-498), with the HTLV-1 and COPD cross-references', 8th edition 2022, V1.03 reprinted with corrections May 2026 (Table 7.39 updated June 2024), https://remotephcmanuals.com.au/document/35499.html, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Before oral prednisolone for longer than 2 weeks (for example in COPD), treat for strongyloides every 3 months while the steroid continues,** alongside TB and hepatitis B screening.
claims.locator: Central Australian Aboriginal Congress, CARPA, CRANAplus and Flinders University (Remote Primary Health Care Manuals), 'CARPA Standard Treatment Manual, 8th edition (e-version V1.03): Worms, Strongyloides testing, treatment and follow-up (pp 494-498), with the HTLV-1 and COPD cross-references', 8th edition 2022, V1.03 reprinted with corrections May 2026 (Table 7.39 updated June 2024), https://remotephcmanuals.com.au/document/35499.html, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Follow up everyone who has been treated.** A person from a high-prevalence area with past strongyloides who is on immune-weakening treatment gets single-dose ivermectin every 3 months. For everyone else, repeat the faeces test at 6 months if symptoms continue, and consult if it is still positive.
claims.locator: Central Australian Aboriginal Congress, CARPA, CRANAplus and Flinders University (Remote Primary Health Care Manuals), 'CARPA Standard Treatment Manual, 8th edition (e-version V1.03): Worms, Strongyloides testing, treatment and follow-up (pp 494-498), with the HTLV-1 and COPD cross-references', 8th edition 2022, V1.03 reprinted with corrections May 2026 (Table 7.39 updated June 2024), https://remotephcmanuals.com.au/document/35499.html, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Asymptomatic eosinophilia (eosinophils 0.7 to 1.5, no gut symptoms or urticaria, not on a drug that causes eosinophilia, not pregnant):** after a medical consult has considered other causes such as atopy, allergy, scabies or medicines, treatment may be advised with albendazole for 3 days plus single-dose ivermectin, taken with full-cream milk or fatty food.
claims.locator: Central Australian Aboriginal Congress, CARPA, CRANAplus and Flinders University (Remote Primary Health Care Manuals), 'CARPA Standard Treatment Manual, 8th edition (e-version V1.03): Worms, Strongyloides testing, treatment and follow-up (pp 494-498), with the HTLV-1 and COPD cross-references', 8th edition 2022, V1.03 reprinted with corrections May 2026 (Table 7.39 updated June 2024), https://remotephcmanuals.com.au/document/35499.html, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Prevention:** keep nails short, wash daily, don't scratch, hot-wash clothes, towels and bedding, and wear shoes so larvae cannot enter through the soles.
